strengths: Well-articulated motivation addressing two genuine problems in vision-language systems: energy-intensive edge-cloud transmission and token explosion from patch-based encoders
Solid systems engineering contributions: 90× speedup with 97% GPU utilization via CUDA optimizations, structured initialization, and luminance-aware pruning strategies
Thoughtful architectural design of GS stem with Fourier encodings, log-scaled covariance representations, and Perceiver Resampler tailored to 2DGS properties
First systematic large-scale study of 2DGS for vision-language alignment, establishing baseline results and identifying bottlenecks for future research
Pragmatic transfer learning approach leveraging frozen RGB backbones minimizes trainable parameters (7%) and computational overhead
Clear presentation with good motivation, informative figures, and sufficient implementation details for reproducibility; commitment to open-source CUDA kernels
weaknesses: Substantial accuracy gap (13-15% vs 18.5% RGB top-1) inadequately explained; no analysis of which semantic information is lost, why gap persists across compression ratios, or visualization of learned representations

Heavy dependence on RGB pre-training undermines core thesis: from-scratch 2DGS training performs substantially worse (Fig. 7), and only 7% of parameters are trained, suggesting 2DGS alone is a weak substrate dependent on RGB representations

Limited experimental scope: single 12.8M DataComp subset, single task (zero-shot ImageNet-1K), no downstream task evaluation, and critically, no comparison with established baselines (JPEG, token pruning methods, other compact representations)

Claimed edge-cloud efficiency benefits not empirically validated: no end-to-end deployment measurements on actual edge devices, no energy/latency comparisons, no analysis of actual overhead of 2DGS fitting and transmission

Incomplete codec pipeline: quantization techniques from GaussianImage (6-bit covariance, residual VQ) acknowledged but not employed; compression ratios reported at float16 precision may misrepresent practical gains with full quantization
Minimal architectural exploration: single backbone variant tested, no ablations on GS stem components, no investigation of architectures designed specifically for 2DGS rather than adapted from RGB

Experimental rigor concerns: no error bars/confidence intervals, single runs without multiple seeds, unclear compression calculation methodology, potential overfitting via validation-based checkpoint selection
Missing critical analysis: no investigation of image types where 2DGS excels/fails, no characterization of visual properties captured vs lost, no failure case visualization

strengths: Clear and well-motivated problem: articulates two real inefficiencies in current vision-language pipelines (bandwidth costs and token explosion)

Solid systems-level engineering: 90× speedup via batch-aware CUDA kernels, structured initialization with pixel-level priors, luminance-aware pruning with L1 regularization, achieving 97% GPU utilization
Novel application: first large-scale study of 2DGS as a learnable substrate for vision-language alignment at 12.8M scale
Pragmatic methodology: transfer learning from RGB backbones while training only 7% of parameters is efficient and reduces computational overhead
Stable results across compression ratios: performance remains consistent from 3× to 12× compression, suggesting robustness of the approach
Thoughtful architectural design: GS stem incorporates Fourier positional encodings, gated sigmoid layers, normalization, and Perceiver Resampler for handling variable-length Gaussian representations
weaknesses: Weak empirical results: 13–15% vs. 18.5% top-1 accuracy represents a substantial 3–5 point gap with no compelling compensation. This degradation is difficult to justify, especially without comparison to related token reduction methods

Critical failure of from-scratch training (Figure 7): dramatic collapse when training 2DGS encoders without RGB initialization strongly suggests fundamental misalignment between 2DGS representations and the downstream learning objective. This is concerning and inadequately addressed

Overstated compression claims: compression ratios (3–23.5×) omit (i) computational cost of fitting 2DGS per image, (ii) Perceiver Resampler bottleneck reducing 400–3136 splats to 196 tokens (~27% of RGB output), and (iii) lack of end-to-end timing/energy/latency measurements despite being a core motivation

Severely limited evaluation scope: single benchmark (ImageNet-1K zero-shot), no downstream task evaluation (VQA, retrieval, captioning), no empirical comparison with related token reduction methods (ToMe, PruMerge, VisionZip) discussed but never tested

Weak baseline: RGB baseline achieves only 18.5% top-1 accuracy with reduced model capacity (38M parameters, 32 epochs). Hard to contextualize whether 2DGS is fundamentally limited or whether the experimental setup is constrained

Insufficient ablation and analysis: no ablations on GS stem components (Fourier encoding, gating mechanisms, normalization), no analysis of what visual information is preserved/lost, missing investigation of why from-scratch training fails, no correlation analysis between 2DGS reconstruction quality and downstream performance

Unjustified architectural choices: Fourier positional encodings for splats, log-scaled covariance, z-score normalization lack principled motivation. Design appears somewhat ad hoc rather than grounded in representation theory

Limited practical impact: Resampler reduces potential compression benefits substantially (196 output tokens), and lack of end-to-end measurements means efficiency claims remain unvalidated. Fitting 2DGS for each image introduces computational overhead not accounted for
Reproducibility concerns: code promised 'soon' but unavailable; hyperparameter choices (differential learning rates) not fully justified; unclear if validation-set tuning was performed

Scaling claims unsupported: 12.8M images and 8 H100 GPUs do not constitute 'large-scale' by modern standards; modern CLIP trains on billions of images. Generalization to realistic training regimes unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real inefficiencies: bandwidth costs for edge-cloud transmission and token explosion in vision-language models with compelling practical motivation

Substantial systems engineering contributions: 90× speedup with 97% GPU utilization through batched CUDA kernels, structured initialization achieving significant PSNR improvements, and luminance-aware pruning strategy that makes large-scale 2DGS training practical
First large-scale systematic study of 2DGS for vision-language alignment on 12.8M DataComp subset, establishing important baselines and identifying architectural bottlenecks
Efficient transfer learning approach training only 7% of parameters while leveraging frozen RGB-pretrained backbones, enabling rapid experimentation
Clear, well-structured presentation with effective motivation, helpful figures, and honest acknowledgment of limitations
Robust performance across compression ratios (3-12×) and splat densities (400-3136), demonstrating that 2DGS retains meaningful semantic information in compact form
weaknesses: Significant unexplained accuracy gap: 2DGS achieves only 13-15% top-1 versus 18.5% RGB top-1 on ImageNet-1K (3-5 point drop), undermining practical viability without root cause analysis or clear path to improvement

Fundamental failure of from-scratch training shown in Figure 7, suggesting 2DGS may not be a viable standalone substrate and instead relies on RGB pretraining, raising questions about the claimed 'native multimodal substrate' narrative

Narrow experimental validation limited to ImageNet-1K zero-shot classification; no evaluation on other multimodal tasks (retrieval, VQA, captioning) or datasets to assess generalization or whether gap persists across domains

Unclear practical efficiency benefits: end-to-end pipeline time not measured, computational cost of 2DGS fitting (~3000 iterations) not quantified, and energy/latency benefits in edge-cloud scenarios remain theorized rather than empirically validated
Quantization techniques from GaussianImage [35] (6-bit covariance, residual vector quantization) omitted from alignment pipeline despite float16 precision limiting actual compression gains

Incomplete architectural justification: GS stem components (Fourier encoding, gating, normalization) appear ad-hoc with no ablation studies isolating their contributions, and design space explicitly stated as 'largely unexplored'
Missing comparative analysis against post-hoc token reduction methods (ToMe, PruMerge, VisionZip) and compression codecs mentioned in related work, limiting claims about relative efficiency

Experimental setup concern: ViT-B width reduced from 716 to 512 for scalability but evidence that 'comparable performance is maintained' not provided, and transfer from RGB-pretrained backbone may unfairly advantage RGB

Limited reproducibility: code promised but not provided, requires full 12.8M DataComp subset and specific hardware (8 H100 GPUs), implementation details sparse on pruning thresholds and regularization weights

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing real inefficiencies in vision-language systems with concrete quantitative evidence (energy consumption, token explosion)
Strong systems engineering contributions: 90× speedup in 2DGS fitting, 97% GPU utilization through batched CUDA kernels, structured initialization, and intelligent pruning strategies
Comprehensive large-scale evaluation on 38 diverse zero-shot benchmarks (natural, fine-grained, synthetic, medical, OCR domains) with extensive ablations and case studies
Technical soundness with clear algorithmic descriptions, detailed implementation details, and strong reproducibility commitment (promised code release)
Honest discussion of limitations including dependency on RGB pretraining, performance drops on distribution-shifted datasets, and lack of GS-native architectures
Solid empirical validation showing 2DGS achieves 90-98% of RGB baseline accuracy with 3-23.5× compression and competitive zero-shot performance on many benchmarks
weaknesses: Fundamental architectural dependency: models require distillation from frozen RGB ViT for effective training; scratch training yields substantially lower accuracy (Appendix Fig. 15). This inverts the core claim—2DGS is an intermediate representation for RGB-pretrained features, not a standalone multimodal substrate

Modest and context-dependent performance trade-offs: average 8-10% relative drop with critical failures on specific domains (diabetic retinopathy: 92% drop, fer2013: 80% drop). Lacks systematic analysis of failure modes and guidance on task applicability

Compression advantages over standard codecs unclear: 5.88× compression for 1600 points is within JPEG range (10-50×). For edge-cloud deployment, must either store GS parameters (defeats purpose) or fit on edge (seconds per image—impractical). End-to-end latency comparison missing

Offline fitting overhead underaddressed: 25.6-53.1 GPU hours to preprocess 12.8M images. 90× speedup is for fitting only; full pipeline cost not contextualized. Real-time/streaming applications infeasible with seconds-per-image fitting

Architecture remains engineered for RGB ViT, not native to 2DGS: Perceiver stem explicitly bridges 2DGS to RGB ViT. Authors admit GS-native architectures remain undiscovered. Point Transformer underperformance (Fig. 19) suggests 2DGS structure poorly suited to point-processing architectures

Incomplete failure analysis: catastrophic performance drops (e.g., diabetic retinopathy 0.08 relative accuracy) lack investigation. No systematic characterization of visual characteristics that 2DGS cannot represent effectively
Baseline fairness: ViT-B/16 (Small) uses non-standard 512 hidden dims; RGB 98-token baseline created via ad-hoc averaging rather than proper retraining (acknowledged in appendix)
Missing comparisons: no empirical evaluation against INR-based approaches, VQ-VAE, or neural codecs despite mentioning them. Limited analysis of why Perceiver outperforms alternative stems

strengths: Large-scale empirical study of 2DGS on 12.8M images with comprehensive zero-shot evaluation across 38 CLIP benchmark datasets
Solid systems engineering: 90× speedup in CUDA kernels with 97% GPU utilization and clear profiling/optimization details
Well-motivated structured initialization showing consistent improvements in convergence speed and PSNR over random initialization
Thorough ablation studies in appendix covering architectural choices (Perceiver vs. alternatives), normalization strategies, distillation losses, and hyperparameters
Honest acknowledgment of critical limitations (RGB pretraining dependency, distribution shift sensitivity, poor from-scratch convergence)
Clear Pareto frontier characterization between compression ratio, accuracy, and token count across multiple model variants
weaknesses: Fundamental architectural limitation: GS models fail to converge from scratch and require RGB-pretrained backbone distillation, contradicting the core claim that 2DGS is 'an alternative visual substrate for alignment'—performance is bounded by RGB teacher quality

Motivation-implementation mismatch: Edge-cloud efficiency motivation emphasizes transmission costs, but the actual pipeline requires offline fitting (25.6–53.1 GPU hours for dataset), leaving the practical deployment scenario unclear and fitting cost unquantified for inference

Compression gains are modest at competitive accuracy: only 3–6× compression at 96–98% of RGB baseline accuracy; for 23.5× compression, accuracy drops to 90–92%, which is not revolutionary compared to JPEG/WebP standards

Serious robustness failures under distribution shift: catastrophic performance degradation on medical images (diabetic_retinopathy: 38.33% → 3.09%) and OOD tasks; paper acknowledges 'sensitivity to sharp distribution shifts' but provides no root-cause analysis or solution

Limited technical novelty: structured initialization, L1+luminance pruning, and two-stage CLIP training are straightforward applications of existing techniques; the contribution is primarily assembly at scale rather than methodological innovation

Experimental fairness issues: RGB baseline uses non-standard ViT-B/16 (width 512 vs. 768) for budget reasons, and 98-token RGB baseline uses post-hoc token merging rather than full retraining; authors acknowledge fairer comparison would be more expensive

Poor from-scratch performance suggests 2DGS lacks native inductive bias for vision-language alignment; the required Perceiver resampler architecture appears to be a workaround rather than a natural fit (alternative architectures underperform)
Token reduction impact is minimal for GS (<2% relative accuracy change from 196→98 tokens), which contradicts one of the two main motivations (token explosion problem) presented in the introduction

No comparison to token pruning/merging baselines (ToMe, VisionZip, FastV, SparseVLM) despite claiming to move 'beyond post-hoc token pruning'; missing analysis of how GS compression compares to simply encoding JPEG bytes

Limited insight into learned representations: no visualization of Gaussian clusters by image type, no analysis of what semantic information is lost at different compression levels, no explanation for why distribution shift causes failures

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing energy costs of edge-cloud RGB transmission and token explosion in VLMs with concrete empirical data

Significant systems-level contributions: 90× speedup for 2DGS fitting with 97% GPU utilization, making large-scale preprocessing practical; structured initialization (grid-based + local color averaging) is well-justified and yields 7 PSNR improvement over random init

Comprehensive large-scale evaluation on 12.8M DataComp images across 38 CLIP benchmark datasets with extensive ablations (distillation losses, normalization strategies, GS-stem architectures), providing thorough empirical validation
Competitive zero-shot results: 3136/1600-point models maintain 96–98% RGB accuracy at 3–6× compression; even 400-point variants preserve 91–92% accuracy; 19/38 datasets best solved by GS variant

Honest and insightful limitations discussion: acknowledges fitting overhead, training-from-scratch failure, RGB-teacher dependence, distribution shift sensitivity, and architectural mismatch with ViTs
Strong reproducibility commitment with promised open-source code and detailed hyperparameter specifications in extensive appendix
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: 2DGS is from prior work (Zhang et al. 2024); structured initialization is straightforward extension for 2D images; two-stage distillation is pragmatic but not architecturally novel; core contribution is systems optimization rather than algorithmic innovation

Fundamental architectural mismatch unresolved: training from scratch severely underperforms (~12% vs. 15% ImageNet-1K after 1 epoch, Fig. 21); requires RGB distillation as workaround, making GS representations dependent on RGB quality; contradicts framing of 'inherently compact, adaptive' substrate

Baseline comparison fairness concerns: RGB 98-token baseline created by averaging patch embeddings post-hoc without retraining; Table 7 shows 5-epoch finetuned RGB-98 achieves 20.56% vs. GS-3136-98 at 19.76% (0.96 relative)—non-negligible gap undermining compression efficiency claims

Missing critical empirical comparisons: no direct benchmarking against token reduction methods (ToMe, PruMerge, VisionZip) extensively discussed in related work; no comparison to JPEG or other codecs; no downstream task evaluation (VQA, captioning) beyond zero-shot classification

Unclear practical value proposition: fitting requires offline preprocessing (not streaming-compatible); data loading speedup is 13× at best; 196→98 token reduction is minor; cost-benefit vs. JPEG + token merging + standard training not rigorously analyzed; edge devices face deployment constraints

Architectural limitations act as band-aid solutions: two-stage training is workaround for poor from-scratch convergence; GS shows increased sensitivity to distribution shift (underperforms on ImageNet-Sketch, FER-2013); suggests fundamental mismatch between Gaussian primitives and ViT learning
